title: ARC-AGI-2 smoke: solve 1 of 5 sealed training tasks
goal: Work the five sealed ARC-AGI-2 training-split tasks in assets/gc-440/task_ids.txt end to end and get at least one task fully solved under cell-exact grading. This is a smoke-scale card: the point is to prove the whole loop -- fetch the pinned task files, study every train pair, write an explicit transformation hypothesis, verify the hypothesis reproduces every train output before touching the test input, emit runs/gc-440/predictions.json in the documented format, run the grader, and re-plan from the grader verdict if the result is short. A task counts only when every test output matches the gold grid exactly, so sloppy almost-right grids are worth nothing.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-440/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 5 task ids, one per line; all from the public training split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-440/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-440/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-440/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-440/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-440/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
